requirements.title: Defined input/output has four direction-and-form characteristic sets for each derived type and kind-parameter set
requirements.definition: For a particular derived type and a particular set of kind type parameter values, there are four possible sets of characteristics for defined input/output procedures: formatted input, formatted output, unformatted input, and unformatted output.

pending.formatted-input-characteristic-set: Compile a conforming READ(FORMATTED) defined I/O specific procedure with the formatted-input dummy sequence and use a formatted input transfer into a sentinel-initialized derived-type variable.
pending.formatted-output-characteristic-set: Compile a conforming WRITE(FORMATTED) defined I/O specific procedure with the formatted-output dummy sequence and use a formatted output transfer of a distinctive derived-type value.
pending.unformatted-input-characteristic-set: Compile a conforming READ(UNFORMATTED) defined I/O specific procedure with the unformatted-input dummy sequence and use an unformatted input transfer into a sentinel-initialized derived-type variable.
pending.unformatted-output-characteristic-set: Compile a conforming WRITE(UNFORMATTED) defined I/O specific procedure with the unformatted-output dummy sequence and use an unformatted output transfer of a distinctive derived-type value.

requirements.title: A program need not supply all four defined input/output procedures
requirements.definition: The program is permitted to supply fewer than all four defined input/output procedures for a derived type and kind-parameter set.

pending.partial-defined-io-procedure-set-permitt: Compile a type that supplies only one conforming defined I/O generic, such as WRITE(FORMATTED), and uses only that matching transfer; the control establishes the procedure was reached through a distinctive output field and does not require unsupported directions/forms.

requirements.title: Defined input/output procedures are specified by interface blocks or generic bindings
requirements.definition: Procedures are specified for derived-type input/output by interface blocks or by generic bindings with a defined-io-generic-spec.

pending.defined-io-interface-block-specification: Compile a module with an INTERFACE WRITE(FORMATTED) block naming a conforming module procedure and verify a formatted transfer reaches it through a distinctive nonblank internal-file result.
pending.defined-io-generic-binding-specification: Compile a type with GENERIC :: WRITE(FORMATTED) => proc and verify a formatted transfer reaches the bound procedure through a distinctive nonblank internal-file result.

requirements.title: Defined-io generic specs map to the four direction-and-form cases
requirements.definition: READ(FORMATTED), READ(UNFORMATTED), WRITE(FORMATTED), and WRITE(UNFORMATTED) are the defined-io-generic-specs for formatted input, unformatted input, formatted output, and unformatted output respectively.

pending.read-formatted-maps-formatted-input: Use a READ(FORMATTED) generic whose procedure changes a derived-type component from a nondefault sentinel during a formatted input transfer.
pending.read-unformatted-maps-unformatted-input: Use a READ(UNFORMATTED) generic whose procedure changes a derived-type component from a nondefault sentinel during an unformatted input transfer.
pending.write-formatted-maps-formatted-output: Use a WRITE(FORMATTED) generic that writes a distinctive nonblank field during a formatted output transfer.
pending.write-unformatted-maps-unformatted-outpu: Use a WRITE(UNFORMATTED) generic that writes a distinctive value during an unformatted output transfer and read it back with nondefault sentinels.

pending.class-dtv-type-spec-form: Compile a conforming extensible defined I/O interface whose dtv dummy has CLASS(t); the paired syntax negative removes the CLASS keyword or parentheses only so parsing reaches R1221.

requirements.title: Extensible dtv types use CLASS and nonextensible dtv types use TYPE
requirements.definition: If derived-type-spec specifies an extensible type, the CLASS keyword shall be used; otherwise, the TYPE keyword shall be used.

pending.extensible-dtv-uses-class: Compile a conforming defined I/O procedure for an extensible type whose dtv dummy uses CLASS(t) and whose transfer reaches the procedure.
pending.nonextensible-dtv-uses-type: Compile a conforming defined I/O procedure for a BIND(C) or SEQUENCE nonextensible type whose dtv dummy uses TYPE(t) and whose transfer reaches the procedure.
pending.extensible-type-keyword-rejected: Diagnostic/control pair changes only CLASS(t) to TYPE(t) for an extensible dtv dummy in an otherwise conforming defined I/O interface.
pending.nonextensible-class-keyword-rejected: Diagnostic/control pair changes only TYPE(t) to CLASS(t) for a nonextensible dtv dummy in an otherwise conforming defined I/O interface.

requirements.title: READ(FORMATTED) procedures have the formatted input dummy characteristics
requirements.definition: A READ(FORMATTED) defined input/output procedure shall have the same characteristics as the formatted input interface: dtv is a dtv-type-spec dummy with INTENT(INOUT), unit is INTEGER INTENT(IN), iotype is CHARACTER(LEN=*) INTENT(IN), v_list is INTEGER INTENT(IN) rank-one array, iostat is INTEGER INTENT(OUT), and iomsg is CHARACTER(LEN=*) INTENT(INOUT).

pending.formatted-read-dtv-inout: Compile and execute a formatted input defined I/O procedure that changes dtv from a nondefault sentinel through INTENT(INOUT).
pending.formatted-read-unit-integer-in: Inside a formatted input defined I/O procedure, copy unit to a saved integer sentinel and use it for a child READ from the parent unit; assert only equality to the parent unit rule when that rule is registered.
pending.formatted-read-iotype-character-in: Inside a formatted input defined I/O procedure, copy iotype into a nonblank module variable and assert the exact LISTDIRECTED, NAMELIST, or DT value owned by 12.6.4.8.3.
pending.formatted-read-v-list-integer-array-in: Use a DT edit descriptor with a nonempty v-list and copy v_list into a sentinel-initialized array; assert size and order after 12.6.4.8.3 p8.
pending.formatted-read-iostat-integer-out: Set iostat to zero after a successful child input transfer; parent IOSTAT= observes zero/nonzero only, never a processor-specific code.
pending.formatted-read-iomsg-character-inout: Initialize parent IOMSG to a nonblank sentinel and have the procedure leave it unchanged when iostat is zero, or set a nonempty message when intentionally returning nonzero; do not compare processor wording.

pending.unformatted-read-dtv-inout: Compile and execute an unformatted input defined I/O procedure that changes dtv from a nondefault sentinel through INTENT(INOUT).

pending.unformatted-read-iostat-integer-out: Set iostat to zero after a successful child unformatted input transfer and observe parent IOSTAT= as zero.
pending.unformatted-read-iomsg-character-inout: Initialize parent IOMSG to a nonblank sentinel and verify the procedure leaves it unchanged for zero iostat or supplies only nonempty text for a deliberate nonzero return.

pending.formatted-write-dtv-in: Pass a derived-type value with distinctive components and have the formatted output procedure write them to a sentinel-filled internal file without modifying dtv.
pending.formatted-write-unit-integer-in: Inside the procedure, use the integer unit dummy for a child WRITE that emits a distinctive nonblank field to the parent file.
pending.formatted-write-iotype-character-in: Copy iotype to output and assert LISTDIRECTED, NAMELIST, or DT text under the matching parent formatting case.
pending.formatted-write-v-list-integer-array-in: Use a DT edit descriptor with a nonempty v-list and emit v_list size/order as decimal fields with exact widths.
pending.formatted-write-iostat-integer-out: Set iostat to zero after successful child output and observe parent IOSTAT= as zero.
pending.formatted-write-iomsg-character-inout: Prefill IOMSG with a nonblank sentinel; for zero iostat verify no change, and for deliberate nonzero verify only that the procedure supplied some message.

accounting.rationale: Mixed definition, permission, and specification mapping split into fine units.
Defines the four direction/form characteristic sets.
Grants latitude not to supply all four procedures.
Defines interface-block and generic-binding specification mechanisms.
Maps each defined-io generic spec to a direction/form case.
Introduces the syntax term used by the following numbered syntax rule.
Grants naming latitude for specific procedures and dummies.

review_rationale: Source registration for 12.6.4.8, defined input/output (batch163). Every unit hash-verified by independent reviewers across two rounds. Round 1 found obligations filed as definitions - the 12.6.4.8.4 resolution rules, and the 12.6.4.8.3 effects that a child data transfer inherits the parent's connection modes, does not position the file, ignores ADVANCE=, associates dtv with the effective item and starts where the file was positioned; all are now requirements with plans in which a DTIO procedure records its observations in module variables with distinguished values. R1221, C1236 and C1237 were pre-accounted. Source accounting only.
